correctness.rationale: Each of the twelve unilateral comparisons in a strict binary three-player game is independently orientable; the resulting best-response graph is exactly an arbitrary orientation of Q3, with no implicit payoff-table identification. The reachability-based weak/connected/super-connected and DAG predicates were reconstructed, including the treatment of sinks, sources, and zero-length paths. The analytic sink-neighborhood proof excludes cyclic equilibrium-bearing nonconnected graphs; the bipartition/source-sink argument excludes acyclic super-connected graphs. Independent complete enumeration of all 4096 orientations reproduces exactly the five class sizes 962,642,888,1220,384, the sink counts 962,2232,844,56,2 and the 112 automorphism orbits; this IS an exhaustive finite proof of the stated finite census, not a sample.
residual_risks: The particular enumeration is only for exactly three binary players; strict ordinal preferences and uniform orientation counting are essential.

value.rationale: The cube Q3 is the complete minimal three-player binary-game orientation model, and connected versus super-connected have explicit implications for adaptive best-response convergence. Exact five-way counts and 112 symmetry-orbits distinguish genuinely different game dynamics and replace Monte Carlo estimates; two finite structural impossibility implications are additional nontrivial content. These are not arbitrary slices of an unknown infinite table.
residual_risks: The result makes no claim for higher-player or non-generic games; future value is a finite benchmark, not a universal dynamics theorem.

limitations: Exact finite strict binary three-player orientation census only; no extrapolation to larger games.
